vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability exists in the swapAndSendMarketing function which uses Address.sendValue() to send BNB to the marketing wallet. If the marketing wallet is a malicious contract that reverts on receiving BNB, the entire swapAndSendMarketing call will revert. This happens during the fee processing in _transfer() when selling tokens to the pair. Since the revert occurs inside inSwapAndLiquify = true block, it will cause the entire sell transaction to revert, preventing the marketing fee from being collected. However, the attacker can set themselves as the marketing wallet (via changeMarketingWallet) and make it revert, then sell tokens without paying marketing fees while other users' transactions fail.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the owner to call changeMarketingWallet() and set marketing wallet to a malicious contract that reverts on receive. 2. Ensure trading is enabled. 3. Accumulate marketing fees in the contract by buying tokens (which adds marketing fees to contract balance). 4. Trigger a sell transaction that will attempt to process fees via swapAndSendMarketing, which will revert due to our malicious marketing wallet. 5. The attacker benefits by avoiding marketing fee payments while still being able to sell tokens (if they're excluded from fees or find another way).
step_by_step_plan: 1. Create a malicious contract that reverts when receiving BNB. 2. Impersonate the owner to enable trading if not already enabled. 3. Impersonate the owner to change marketing wallet to our malicious contract. 4. Buy some tokens to accumulate marketing fees in the contract. 5. Wait until contract token balance >= swapTokensAtAmount. 6. Sell tokens to trigger the fee processing, which will revert at swapAndSendMarketing. 7. The attacker can potentially sell without paying marketing fees if they're excluded from fees or if the revert prevents fee collection entirely.
